proof.text: For each small quasicategory Q write $\Phi_Q$ for postcomposition by F on cores. Take Q=\mathcal B. The identity vertex of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)^\simeq$ has a preimage together with a path to it because $\Phi_{\mathcal B}$ is an equivalence of spaces (equivalently, its homotopy fiber over the identity is contractible). Calling the preimage G gives a coherent functor $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and an equivalence edge $\alpha:FG\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$ in the functor quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, mapping-space criterion; archived source WANTED

proof.text: Whisker $\alpha$ on the right by F, that is, precompose it with F: the edge $\alpha:\mathcal B\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal B$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)$ gives $\alpha F=\alpha\circ(F\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}):\mathcal A\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal B$, an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ from $FGF$ to $F$; restriction along $F\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n}$ in each degree is a simplicial map $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$. By the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], every vertex component $\alpha_b$ is an equivalence of $\mathcal B$ because $\alpha$ is an equivalence edge; the component of $\alpha F$ at $a\in\mathcal A$ is $\alpha_{F(a)}$, so by the same criterion $\alpha F:FGF\simeq F$ is a coherent natural equivalence, i.e. an edge of the core $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)^\simeq$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, compatibility of mapping-space composition; archived source WANTED

proof.text: Now take Q=\mathcal A. The map $\Phi_{\mathcal A}:\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal A)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes (cores are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]), so it is bijective on path components of the realizations. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] the simplicial components of a Kan complex (vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges) map bijectively and naturally to these path components, so $\Phi_{\mathcal A}$ is bijective on simplicial components. Its vertices $GF$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ map to $FGF$ and $F$, which are joined by the edge $\alpha F$ of step 2; hence $GF$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ are joined by a finite zigzag of edges of the Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal A)^\simeq$. Filling horns $\Lambda^2_0,\Lambda^2_2$ reverses an edge and filling $\Lambda^2_1$ composes two edges, so there is a single edge $\eta:GF\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ of the core. Every edge of the core is an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal A)$, so $\eta:GF\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ is a coherent natural equivalence, not merely an equality of components.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, converse test with Q=\mathcal A; archived source WANTED

proof.text: The functor G together with the coherent natural equivalences $\eta:GF\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and $\alpha:FG\simeq\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$ is precisely the data required for F to be a functor equivalence under the definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The construction uses the core tests to retain all higher coherences, so the stated coherent quasi-inverse and both natural equivalences follow.

title: Functor equivalence detected by all core functor-category tests
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories, cores and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor between small quasicategories. Suppose that for every small quasicategory $Q$, postcomposition induces an equivalence of spaces $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal A)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal B)^\simeq$. Then $F$ is a functor equivalence. In particular, taking $Q=\mathcal B$ and $Q=\mathcal A$ supplies a coherent quasi-inverse and the two natural equivalences.
